(1840) }} }} }} '''''Eustoma russellianum''''' is a species of flowering plant in the [[gentian family]]. One of its previous [[binomial name]]s was ''Eustoma grandiflorum''. Common names include '''showy prairie gentian''', '''prairie gentian''', '''Texas bluebells''', '''Texas bluebell''', '''bluebell''',{{NPIN|EUEXR|''Eustoma exaltatum'' ssp. ''russellianum''}} and '''Lisianthus'''. There is a cultivar, 'Bolero Deep Blue'.{{cite web |url=http://www.flowercouncil.org/uk/news/fpnews/Productnieuws2002/NPlant_May02.asp |title=Eustoma russellianum: Novelty Plant of the Month for May 2002 |date=2002-05-01 |publisher=Flower Council of Holland |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071007052635/http://www.flowercouncil.org/uk/news/fpnews/Productnieuws2002/NPlant_May02.asp |archive-date=2007-10-07}} ==Description== ''Eustoma russellianum'' has blue-green waxy leaves and showy bell shaped flowers in blue pink or white each borne singly on an upright plant. Depending on growing conditions it may present as an annual, biennial, or perennial plant. ==Distribution and habitat== It is found primarily in the [[Great Plains]] region of North America, from Wyoming southeast to Nebraska, and south to Texas and Mexico. Due to its popularity and the frequency with which it is picked, it has been unable to naturally reseed itself in its native distribution. It prefers moist, sandy soils and often grows near streams, creek-beds, moist meadows, and springs. ==Cultivation== Prairie gentian is a popular garden flower, and has been cultivated in Japan for over 70 years. Many varieties, including those with double petals, or a variety of colored flowers, have been developed. It is not often attempted in native wildflower gardens due to its high moisture requirements and short lifespan.{{cite book |last1=Barr |first1=Claude A. |title=Jewels of the plains : wild flowers of the Great Plains grasslands and hills |date=1983 |publisher=University of Minnesota Press |location=Minneapolis |isbn=0-8166-1127-0 |pages=79–80}} ==Diseases==
